$comment: What Larva links from C, hand-rolls, or plans to link — and the SDK names that would replace it. `make sdk-diff` tests each `match` regex (case-insensitive) against every NEW package id (`core:crypto/tls`) and every NEW symbol as `pkg.name` (`core:sys/windows.GetPriorityClass`), and lists hits under 'Candidates'. A hit is a lead for the reuse scout (CLAUDE.md §2), not a verdict: `why` says what a replacement must keep. Hand-declared foreign procs need no entry here; sdk-diff finds those by name on its own. Add an entry in the PR that adds the dependency or the hand-rolled code.

entries.why: Client and server TLS for fetch/net/https. Stage 2 (#6) needs ClientHello control matching Chrome's fingerprint — a replacement must expose extension order, GREASE, cipher and group lists, ALPN and session resumption, and serve tls.createServer too.
Loading the OS root store; Windows goes through Crypt32 by hand.
Content-Encoding: zstd, decoded off the loop. Needs streaming decode with a window cap and no growth past the declared size (pinned by the zstd no-growth test).
Content-Encoding: br. Needs streaming decode and Chrome's error behaviour on truncated input.
gzip/deflate bodies. vendor:zlib is the C library; a pure-Odin inflate replaces it only with a `make bench` number at least as good and Chrome's raw-deflate sniff kept.
HTTP/1.x request/response head parsing for http/net. Vendored for throughput (CLAUDE.md §2); a replacement must match picohttpparser on `make bench-http`.
Not linked yet — an SDK HTTP/2 or HPACK implementation changes the #7 plan. Must allow Chrome's SETTINGS/WINDOW_UPDATE/priority fingerprint.
Incremental HTML parsing with pause/resume at <script>; must follow the WHATWG tree builder.
Design reference only: Lava's loop owns phases and timers with Node semantics. Read new nbio work before changing the loop.

entries.ours: js/internal/url.js; pkg/http/cookie (hand-rolled RFC 6265bis jar, #9; vendored Public Suffix List compiled by scripts/gen-psl.mjs into a sorted table)
entries.why: WHATWG URL stays in JS. The cookie jar parses Set-Cookie as Chrome 158 does (tests/dom cookie-document-*.page, tests/web cookie-*): a replacement parser must keep Chrome's refusals (any CTL, HTAB inside a name or value), case-insensitive prefixes, '+' in Max-Age and the 4096/1024/180-to-150 limits. A public suffix list in the SDK could replace psl.odin's table only if it matches Chrome's registry rules (unlisted TLD = one label, a wildcard's parent is a suffix, PRIVATE rules included; pkg/http/cookie/psl_test.odin) and costs no more than a binary search over rodata.

entries.ours: pkg/http/cookie/punycode.odin (hand-rolled RFC 3492 encoder + lowercase-only UTS-46 for Domain=)
entries.why: No IDNA in core:/vendor: at the pin; libidn2 is runtime-only on Ubuntu (no headers). An SDK IDNA with full UTS-46 mapping would also lift domain_to_ascii's deviation (inputs needing more than lowercasing are refused).
